summary: Killed the injection class on the harness ps1 + autorevise-py surface. S1 (unquoted-interpolation): generalized the safeName point-fix into a dot-sourced Sanitize-SQ helper (harness/lib/quote-safe.ps1) + python twin, and routed all 9 uncontrolled interpolations in orchestrate.ps1's launch runner through it; the dry run now writes the real runner BOM-free so it is parseable. S8 (BOM): repaired the one committed JSON that failed json.load (resolved_lines.json) + swapped its producer to Write-Utf8NoBom; harness JSON census now 371/0. findings.claim: CONFIG-LOW-RISK BOM writers left as-is, documented not hidden. drive_autoresearch.ps1:136, _idle_control.ps1:27/53, dispatch_lock_control.ps1:48 write a UTF-8 BOM but to runtime-only lock/TEMP/pointer files read back by BOM-tolerant PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json - never a committed *.json, never a python json.load consumer. harness/retired/run_followon.ps1:64 carries the identical S1 class (leg.id/leg.wt into a runner here-string) but is under harness/retired/ - frozen, not live-dispatched. Recorded, not touched (never-rebuild-shipped-code).

harness/run.ts is the S1 ORIGIN surface (0522ad0e backslash-eaten path; 943e5375 2000-char brief split) but is .ts - outside this leg's sweep globs (harness/**/*.ps1 + harness/autorevise/**/*.py). Already uses delivery-by-file-reference. A TypeScript quoting lint is filed as a spawn.

The test harness itself hit BOTH classes during development, confirming they are real and subtle: (S1) the PS driver's -Manifest param collided case-insensitively with orchestrate's [string]$manifest and silently coerced the parsed object back to a string (variable shadowing); (S8) Get-Content read a BOM-less UTF-8 manifest as ANSI, mangling unicode names. Both fixed in the test (ReadAllText + unique param name + file-based UTF-8 transfer).
